title: Decomposition by the isomorphism type of the model
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme and $\Lambda$ a discrete commutative ring. Write $\Lambda_X$ for the constant sheaf of rings on the small pro-etale site $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Let $F$ be a locally constant $\Lambda_X$-module sheaf [def-weil-proetale-locally-constant-sheaf] of finite presentation: it admits a pro-etale trivializing covering whose constant module models are finitely presented $\Lambda$-modules (a finitely presented module is a cokernel of a map $\Lambda^m\to\Lambda^n$ with $m,n$ finite). Fix a set $R$ containing exactly one representative of each isomorphism class of such modules. Then $X=\coprod_{M\in R}X_M$ is a disjoint union of open and closed subschemes, with the open subscheme structure [def-weil-open-immersion], such that, for each $M$, the restriction $F|_{X_M}$ is pro-etale locally isomorphic to the constant module sheaf $\underline M$.

proof.text:
For a set $E$ put $C_E=
u_X^*\underline E_{X,\mathrm{et}}$. This is the constant pro-etale sheaf with value $E$. Indeed the comparison adjunction and the constant-sheaf adjunction give, naturally in a pro-etale sheaf of sets $G$,
$\operatorname{Hom}(C_E,G)=\operatorname{Hom}(\underline E_{X,\mathrm{et}},
u_{X,*}G)=\operatorname{Map}(E,(
u_{X,*}G)(X))=\operatorname{Map}(E,G(X))$.
The last equality is the explicit direct-image formula at the identity object in [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. By [lem-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf-maps-global-sections] the constant pro-etale sheaf has this same universal property. The maps in both directions corresponding to their coefficient sections are inverse: either composite fixes every coefficient section, hence is the identity by that universal property. This fixes the identification canonically on constants.

source.place: Tag 0H7J, example-constant-sheaf; comparison adjunction at the final object

proof.text:
For every object $f:V\to X$ of $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$, [lem-cbc-comparison-pullback-sections] gives
$C_E(V)=\Gamma(V_{\mathrm{et}},f_{\mathrm{et}}^{-1}\underline E_{X,\mathrm{et}})$.
Use [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-constant-sheaf] to identify the sheaf on the right with $\underline E_{V,\mathrm{et}}$, carrying each coefficient section to the same coefficient section. Thus $C_E(V)\cong\underline E_{V,\mathrm{et}}(V)$. The comparison section formula specifies restriction along every pro-etale arrow, and the constant-sheaf pullback identification is unique with this normalization, so these bijections commute with restriction and with maps of coefficient sets.

Apply [lem-galois-constant-sheaf-sets-representable] with base $V$ and arbitrary set $E$: the last set in step 2 is the set of $V$-morphisms $V\to\coprod_E V$, sending a coefficient $e$ to the $e$-coprojection. By [lem-galois-coproduct-copies-morphisms-clopen] these are exactly the maps $|V|\to E$ whose fibres are open, equivalently the Zariski-locally constant maps. A coefficient section is the constant function with that value. Restriction along $g:W\to V$ is composition with $|g|$: on every open fibre of the locally constant map the section is a coefficient section; after pullback it remains that coefficient by step 2, and those inverse-image opens cover $W$. Uniqueness in the sheaf condition therefore gives this formula. Consequently
$C_E(V)=\operatorname{LC}(|V|,E)$ naturally in $V$ and $E$.
For module coefficients the addition and scalar operations are pointwise: they agree on constant local sections and hence on their open coverings. In particular the constant module sheaves used below restrict to the constant module models on every localized site.

source.place: Tag 03P5, remark-constant-locally-constant-maps (the argument does not use a group law); Groupoids Tag 03YW, example-constant-group

proof.text: Choose a trivializing covering $\{u_i:U_i\to X\}_{i\in I}$ and finitely presented models $N_i$ as in the hypothesis and [def-weil-proetale-locally-constant-sheaf]. For each $i$ choose the unique representative $M_i\in R$ isomorphic to $N_i$ and replace the trivialization by its composite with that module isomorphism, obtaining $e_i:\underline{M_i}|_{U_i}\xrightarrow{\sim}F|_{U_i}$. Restricting again to $U_i\times_XU_j$ gives two trivializations of the same sheaf: restriction is sectionwise and relocalizes as specified in [def-pur-localized-ringed-site].

source.place: paragraph 1: choose local isomorphisms instead of presenting their epimorphism

proof.text:
If a nonempty object $W\to X$ has isomorphisms $\underline M|_W\cong F|_W\cong\underline{M'}|_W$ with $M,M'\in R$, compose them to obtain inverse morphisms $a,b$ between the two constant sheaves. Clause 2 of [det-pe-finite-local-systems-hom], applied to the finitely presented modules $M,M'$, identifies $a$ and $b$ with sections of the constant Hom sheaves. By steps 1--3 these sections are locally constant functions
$|W|\to\operatorname{Hom}_\Lambda(M,M')$ and $|W|\to\operatorname{Hom}_\Lambda(M',M)$.
That clause is compatible with composition; hence at any point $w\in|W|$ the two values satisfy $b(w)a(w)=1_M$ and $a(w)b(w)=1_{M'}$. They are inverse module maps. Thus $M\cong M'$, and the representative condition gives $M=M'$. In particular, if $M_i\ne M_j$ then $U_i\times_XU_j$ is empty. No connectedness or finiteness of the underlying sets of the modules is used.

source.place: Models are locally unique; expanded using the listed Hom-sheaf lemma instead of a geometric-point evaluation

proof.text: For each $i$ take the coefficient section $s_i=M_i$ of the sheaf $C_R$ over $U_i$. These sections agree on $U_i\times_XU_j$: if that object is nonempty step 5 gives $M_i=M_j$; if it is empty its set of sections is a singleton, since the empty covering of the empty scheme is a pro-etale covering by the fpqc definition [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering]. The equalizer condition defining a sheaf [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] now gives a unique section $\sigma\in C_R(X)$ with $\sigma|_{U_i}=s_i$. This is the blueprint's type-map descent, expressed directly on a chosen trivializing covering; it requires neither objectwise surjectivity of an epimorphism nor a pointwise formula for a sheaf coproduct.

source.place: The type map: descent of the compatible local type labels

proof.text: Under step 3 at $V=X$, let $t:|X|\to R$ be the locally constant function corresponding to $\sigma$, and put $X_M=t^{-1}(M)$ with its open subscheme structure [def-weil-open-immersion]. These opens cover and are pairwise disjoint, and $X\setminus X_M=\bigcup_{M'\ne M}X_{M'}$ is open, so each is closed as well; this is also the clopen decomposition in [lem-galois-coproduct-copies-morphisms-clopen]. The coproduct $Y=\coprod_M X_M$ exists by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family]. The inclusions define $Y\to X$. On underlying spaces this is the bijection from the disjoint union of the open pieces onto their union, a homeomorphism since each piece is open. On each piece its map on structure sheaves is the identity restriction of $\mathcal O_X$, so it is an isomorphism of locally ringed spaces and hence of schemes. Thus the claimed decomposition is a scheme coproduct, including empty pieces and an infinite indexing set.

source.place: The type map: fibres of the global locally constant type function

proof.text: Fix $M\in R$. Base change of the chosen covering gives a pro-etale covering $\{W_i=U_i\times_X X_M\to X_M\}_i$ by the site axiom in [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. On $W_i$ the restriction of $\sigma$ is the coefficient $M_i$ by step 6. By the restriction-as-composition formula in step 3 it is also the coefficient $M$, since the map to $X$ factors through $X_M$. If $W_i$ is nonempty, evaluation of these equal constant functions at a point gives $M_i=M$; the restriction of $e_i$ is therefore a trivialization by $\underline M$. If $W_i$ is empty, its module sheaf has exactly one section (the zero module) and the unique map between any two such module sheaves is an isomorphism. Restricting the $e_i$ as in [def-pur-localized-ringed-site] supplies the required trivializations on this covering. This proves the conclusion also when $X_M$ or $X$ is empty.
